title: Singapore Airlines Plans 'Largest Double Bed in the Sky'
paragraphs: For most of us, getting a good night's sleep on a plane can be difficult. But Singapore Airlines is hoping to change that — at least for passengers who can pay for a little luxury.
The airline plans to spend more than $1.5 billion on new cabins for its long-distance flights. And the biggest attraction is what it calls "the largest double bed in the sky."

In first class, two seats next to each other will turn into a bed that's 203 centimeters long and 152 centimeters wide — the same size as a standard US queen bed. When passengers aren't sleeping, the seats can become a sofa for two. Each first-class cabin will also have sliding doors and 32-inch entertainment screens.
Business-class passengers will also get sliding doors and seats that turn into flat beds. Some neighboring seats will let couples sleep side by side, too.

And people flying in economy won't be forgotten. They'll get more legroom, better headrests and extra space for their bags. The airline said it would also offer better in-flight entertainment, more meal options and high-speed internet.
The changes will be made to 72 planes over time, beginning in the second half of 2027.

The expensive makeover comes as airlines try to win over travelers who are happy to pay more for a better flying experience. Air France, British Airways and other companies are also spending billions on luxury cabins.

With fuel costs going up, some travelers are choosing to stay home rather than pay higher ticket prices. But demand for more expensive seats has stayed strong, giving airlines another reason to focus on wealthier travelers.
And if you're flying economy, here's hoping the new headrests do the trick!
